q: Advance payment against stores bills can be made up to:

options.A: 90% of the bill amount
options.B: 95% of the bill amount
options.D: 100% of the bill amount in all cases

e: Advance payment against stores bills is permitted up to 98% of the bill amount, the balance being retained until the material is finally accepted and all dues are adjusted.

q: A debit balance under 'Purchase Suspense' indicates:

options.A: Material received but bills not paid
options.B: Bills paid but material not received
options.C: Material issued to shops but not paid for
options.D: Excess stock held in depots

e: A debit under Purchase Suspense means money has gone out (bills paid) but the corresponding material has not yet been received and taken into stock, so the amount awaits linking with receipts.

q: 'Sales Suspense' is credited when:

options.A: Scrap is surveyed off
options.B: The purchaser deposits the sale value with the Railways
options.C: Stores are issued to a workshop
options.D: A rate contract is finalised

e: Sales Suspense is credited when the purchaser deposits the sale value with the Railways, because the amount is held in suspense until the sold material is actually delivered to him.

q: Stores are treated as 'dead surplus' when they have:

options.A: Not been issued for 12 months and are not expected to be used in the next 12 months
options.B: Not been used for 24 months and are not expected to be used in the next 24 months
options.C: Become obsolete due to a change in design
options.D: Been declared surplus by the depot officer at any time

e: Stores become dead surplus when they have not been issued for 24 months and are not expected to be used during the next 24 months, i.e. they are lying idle with no foreseeable demand.

q: Turnover Ratio (TOR) of stores is computed as:

options.A: Total issues divided by closing balance
options.B: Closing balance divided by total issues
options.C: Total receipts divided by total issues
options.D: Average stock divided by annual consumption

e: Turnover Ratio (TOR) = Closing balance / Total issues. A higher ratio means more stock is held relative to issues, indicating more capital locked up in inventory.

q: The difference between the sale value and the book value of scrap sold is booked to:

options.A: Purchase Suspense
options.B: Traffic Suspense
options.D: Depreciation Reserve Fund

e: Scrap is sold at its market sale value while the books carry it at book value; the difference between the two is a value difference in stores accounts and is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: The Stores Budget of a railway is described as a 'derived' budget because:

options.A: It is prepared by the Railway Board directly
options.B: Its requirements are derived from the works and maintenance programmes of the consuming departments
options.D: It is merged with the Capital Budget

e: The Stores Budget is called 'derived' because stores requirements are not assessed independently; they flow from the works, maintenance and operation programmes of the departments that consume the stores.

q: ABC analysis of inventory is carried out on the basis of:

options.A: Physical quantity of items in stock
options.B: Annual consumption value of the items
options.D: Date of last purchase

e: ABC analysis ranks items by their annual consumption value (annual usage x unit price), so that A items - few in number but high in value - get the tightest control.

q: Issues of stores to revenue (working expense) heads are linked to which Primary Unit of expenditure?

options.A: PU 11
options.B: PU 27
options.D: PU 35

e: Stores issued to revenue working expenses are charged under Primary Unit 27, which is the primary unit prescribed for stores (material) in the classification of revenue expenditure.

q: Physical verification of stores balances on Railways is carried out by:

options.A: The depot storekeeper himself
options.B: Stock Verifiers of the Accounts Department
options.C: The Travelling Inspector of Stores only
options.D: The consignee departments

e: Physical verification is done by Stock Verifiers of the Accounts Department, an agency independent of the custodian, so that the check on stock balances is impartial.

q: A credit balance under 'Purchase Suspense' indicates:

options.A: Bills paid but material not received
options.B: Material received but bills not yet paid
options.C: Material issued to shops in excess of demand
options.D: Stores written off after stock verification

e: A credit balance under Purchase Suspense means material has been received into stock but the supplier's bill has not yet been paid, so the liability awaits settlement.

q: A debit balance under 'Sales Suspense' indicates:

options.A: Sale value deposited by the purchaser but the material/scrap not yet delivered to him
options.B: Scrap surveyed off but not yet put to auction
options.C: Stores sold but sale value not yet deposited by the purchaser
options.D: Excess stock found during stock verification

e: A debit under Sales Suspense arises where the sale value has been deposited by the purchaser but delivery of the material has not yet been effected, so final adjustment is pending.

q: The Stock Adjustment Account is operated to adjust differences arising in stores accounts on account of:

options.A: Price (value) differences only
options.B: Quantity differences only
options.D: Differences in freight charges only

e: The Stock Adjustment Account absorbs both kinds of stores differences - those in quantities found on verification and those in value arising from rate revisions and pricing differences.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A stock sheet is prepared only when a shortage is found in stock verification, and not for an excess.
2. Shortages found in stock verification are recovered from the stockholder.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: a stock sheet is prepared for every difference found, whether shortage or excess. Statement 2 is true: shortages are recovered from the stockholder responsible for the custody of the stores.

q: Procedural irregularities noticed during stock verification are brought out by the Inspector of Stores Accounts (ISA)/Assistant Stock Verifier through:

options.A: An error sheet
options.B: A narrative report
options.D: A muster roll

e: Procedural irregularities (as distinct from quantity differences shown in stock sheets) are reported by the ISA/Assistant Stock Verifier through a narrative report to the competent authority.

q: In stores inventory control, the abbreviation AAC stands for:

options.A: Annual Average Consumption
options.B: Average Annual Consumption
options.D: Approved Annual Ceiling

e: AAC stands for Average Annual Consumption - the average yearly consumption of an item, which forms the basis for fixing coverage and quantities to be procured.

q: After the model SOP of 2018, vetting of AAC by Headquarters Finance is required only for:

options.A: B-category items
options.B: C-category items
options.D: All categories of items

e: After the model SOP of 2018, Headquarters Finance vetting of AAC is confined to A-category (high-value) items, where financial scrutiny matters most.

q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised source of supply of stores under the Stores Code (Vol. I, Para 201)?

options.A: Purchases through tenders and contracts
options.B: Manufacture in railway workshops
options.C: Transfers from other stores depots and returns to stores
options.D: Confiscation of a defaulting contractor's material

e: Confiscation of a defaulting contractor's material is not a recognised source of supply under Para 201 of the Stores Code; supplies come only through purchases, manufacture and transfers/returns.

q: A rate (running) contract in stores purchase is an arrangement under which:

options.A: A fixed quantity is supplied in one lot at a fixed price
options.B: Stores are supplied on demand at a fixed rate, irrespective of the quantity ordered
options.C: Rates are revised after every supply
options.D: Supply is made only against advance cash payment

e: A rate (running) contract fixes only the rate; stores are drawn on demand during its currency, the quantity actually ordered varying with requirement.

q: Proprietary articles covered by a Proprietary Article Certificate (PAC) are procured through:

options.A: Open tender
options.B: Single tender
options.D: Reverse auction

e: Proprietary articles are available from a single source only, as certified by the PAC, so they are necessarily procured through single tender from that source.

q: On Indian Railways, reverse auction (on IREPS) is used for:

options.A: Disposal of scrap
options.B: Purchase of stores
options.D: Award of catering contracts

e: On IREPS, reverse auction is a purchase tool in which approved bidders compete downwards in price for supply contracts; scrap disposal is done through forward e-auction.

q: Where a supplier fails to supply the ordered stores, the Railway may make a 'risk purchase', which means purchasing the stores from another source:

options.A: At the risk and cost of the defaulting supplier
options.B: At the risk and cost of the Railway itself
options.C: Without any tender, at the highest quoted rate
options.D: Only from Government undertakings

e: Risk purchase means buying the stores from another source at the risk and cost of the defaulting supplier, so any extra cost is recoverable from him.

q: In stores tenders, firms registered with NSIC/MSME (and RDSO-approved sources) are, as a rule, exempted from payment of:

options.A: Security Deposit
options.B: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD)
options.D: Inspection charges

e: NSIC/MSME-registered and RDSO-approved firms are exempted from Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) in stores tenders, as a measure to encourage small enterprises and proven sources.

q: The minimum percentage of annual procurement of goods and services to be made from Micro and Small Enterprises (MSMEs) is:
e: Under the public procurement policy for MSEs, a minimum of 25% of annual procurement of goods and services must be made from Micro and Small Enterprises.

q: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, a 'Class-I local supplier' is one whose local content is at least:
e: Under the Make in India Order, a Class-I local supplier is one with local content of at least 50%, which qualifies him for purchase preference.

q: In the sale of scrap by e-auction, the balance of the sale value is payable by the purchaser within:

options.A: 10 days
options.B: 21 days
options.D: 40 days

e: In scrap e-auction, after paying the earnest money/sale deposit, the purchaser must pay the balance of the sale value within 40 days of the auction.

q: A 'deduct entry' is provided in the Stores Budget in order to:

options.A: Provide for depreciation of stores in stock
options.B: Prevent double budgeting of the value of stores drawn for works and maintenance
options.D: Meet the cost of stock verification

e: The deduct entry in the Stores Budget neutralises the value of stores drawn for works and maintenance, which is already provided in the respective works/demands, thus preventing double budgeting.

q: The statement of the Stock Adjustment Account is annexed to the:

options.A: Budget Estimates
options.B: Appropriation Accounts
options.C: Finance Accounts of the Central Government
options.D: Works Register

e: The statement of the Stock Adjustment Account, showing the differences adjusted during the year, is annexed to the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways.

q: The 'fall clause' in a stores contract provides that:

options.A: The contract automatically terminates if prices fall in the market
options.B: If the contractor sells or offers the same item to any other buyer at a lower rate during the currency of the contract, the lower rate shall apply to the railway contract also
options.C: The Railway may reduce the ordered quantity without notice
options.D: Payment falls due only after final inspection

e: The fall clause protects the Railway: if the contractor sells the same item to any other buyer at a lower rate during the contract, that lower rate applies to the Railway's supplies too.

q: The Priced Stores Ledger (Price Ledger) of a stores depot primarily records:

options.A: Only the names of approved suppliers
options.B: Only the physical quantities of stores, without any value
options.C: The prices (book value) at which stores transactions are accounted for
options.D: The tender notices issued during the year

e: The Priced Stores Ledger (Price Ledger) records the book (issue) prices/rates of items, at which all receipts, issues and balances are valued in the priced accounts.

q: The Bin Card maintained at a stores depot records:

options.A: Quantities of stores received, issued and in balance, without values
options.B: Only the values of stores, without quantities
options.C: Both quantities and values of all transactions
options.D: Names and addresses of approved suppliers

e: The Bin Card is a purely numerical (quantity) record kept at the bin, showing receipts, issues and the balance in hand, without any values.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Priced Stores Ledger records both the quantities and the values of stores transactions.
2. The Bin Card records quantities only.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the Priced Stores Ledger carries quantities with values for accounting, while the Bin Card at the depot records quantities only.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Stock items' are items regularly stocked in depots to meet day-to-day requirements.
2. 'Non-stock items' are procured against specific demands and are not ordinarily stocked.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: stock items are regularly stocked in depots for day-to-day needs, while non-stock items are bought against specific demands and not ordinarily stocked.

q: Every stock item held in a railway stores depot is identified by a:

options.A: Voucher number
options.B: PL (Price Ledger) Number
options.D: GeM catalogue number

e: Every stock item is identified by a PL (Price Ledger) Number, the uniform codification under which it is stocked and accounted for in all depots.

q: A Receipt Note is prepared by a stores depot when:

options.A: Material is received, inspected and accepted into stock
options.B: Material is issued to a consuming department
options.C: A purchase order is placed on a firm
options.D: Scrap is delivered to a purchaser

e: A Receipt Note is prepared when material received is inspected and accepted into stock; it is the basic document for taking the material on account and paying the supplier.

q: Before a supplier's stores bill is passed for payment, the Accounts office links it with:

options.A: The receipt note only
options.B: The purchase order only
options.D: The purchase order, the receipt note and the bill together

e: A bill is passed only after three-way linking - with the purchase order (terms and rate), the receipt note (material actually received and accepted) and the bill itself.

q: Stores issued from a depot to a consuming department are priced at:

options.A: The current market price on the date of issue
options.B: The rate quoted in the last tender
options.C: The book value (issue price) as per the Priced Stores Ledger
options.D: A rate fixed by the consuming department

e: Issues are priced at the book value (issue price) recorded in the Priced Stores Ledger, not at fluctuating market prices, ensuring uniformity in stores accounting.

q: A Stores Tender Committee dealing with high-value purchases includes a member from the:

options.A: Personnel Department
options.B: Finance/Accounts Department
options.D: Security (RPF) Department

e: For high-value purchases the Tender Committee includes a Finance/Accounts member so that financial propriety and reasonableness of rates are examined before acceptance.

q: Stores purchase contracts on Indian Railways are governed by the:

options.A: IRS (Indian Railway Standard) Conditions of Contract
options.B: General Conditions of Contract for works
options.C: Indian Contract Act alone, with no standard conditions
options.D: Conditions printed on the GeM portal only

e: Stores purchase contracts are governed by the IRS (Indian Railway Standard) Conditions of Contract, which lay down the standard terms for supply contracts on Railways.

q: A 'limited tender' for stores is invited from:

options.A: Any firm responding to a press advertisement
options.B: A single firm chosen by the depot officer
options.D: A limited number of approved/registered firms

e: A limited tender is invited only from a limited number of approved/registered firms, unlike an open tender advertised to all.

q: In the two-bid (two-packet) system of tendering:

options.A: Both packets are opened together and the lowest rate is accepted
options.B: The price packet is opened first and the technical packet later
options.C: Price bids of only those bidders who qualify in the techno-commercial bid are opened
options.D: Negotiation is compulsory with all bidders

e: In the two-packet system, the techno-commercial bids are evaluated first; price bids are opened only for bidders who qualify technically, keeping price from influencing technical evaluation.

q: The 'price variation clause' in a stores contract is meant to cover:

options.A: Variation in the quantity ordered by the Railway
options.B: Variation in the prices of inputs and statutory levies during the currency of the contract
options.D: Variation in the place of delivery

e: The price variation clause adjusts the contract price for changes in input costs and statutory levies occurring during the currency of the contract.

q: The 'book examination clause' in a stores contract entitles the Railway to:

options.A: Examine the books of account of the contractor to verify the costs and prices claimed
options.B: Examine the personal bank account of the contractor's proprietor
options.C: Stop all payments to the contractor without notice
options.D: Take over the contractor's factory for inspection

e: The book examination clause empowers the Railway to inspect the contractor's books to verify the costs and prices claimed by him under the contract.

q: The 'option clause' in a purchase order permits the Railway to:

options.A: Cancel the order at any time without notice
options.B: Change the specification of the material after supply
options.C: Transfer the order to another firm
options.D: Order an additional quantity on the same terms and conditions during the currency of the contract

e: The option clause allows the Railway to order an additional quantity (over and above the ordered quantity) on the same rates and terms during the currency of the contract.

q: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) in stores tenders is subject to a maximum ceiling of:

options.A: Rs 10 lakh
options.B: Rs 25 lakh
options.D: Rs 1 crore

e: Earnest Money Deposit in stores tenders is capped at a maximum of Rs 50 lakh, so that bidders are not burdened with excessive deposits in very large tenders.

q: Emergency purchases of stores may be made without following the normal tender procedure:

options.A: In emergent situations, by the competent stores authority, for recorded reasons
options.B: By any storekeeper at his own discretion
options.D: Only at the end of the financial year

e: Emergency purchases without normal tendering are permitted only in genuine emergent situations, by the competent stores authority, with the reasons recorded.

q: Indents/requisitions for procurement of stores are vetted by Finance principally to ensure:

options.A: That the lowest tenderer is selected
options.B: Availability of funds and the propriety of the demand
options.C: That the material is inspected by RDSO
options.D: That the supplier is registered with NSIC

e: Finance vetting of indents ensures that funds are available for the purchase and that the demand itself is proper and justified, before procurement is set in motion.

q: Bills for purchases made through the GeM portal are processed through the portal, which is linked with the Railways':

options.A: HRMS
options.B: e-Office
options.D: IPAS

e: Bills for GeM purchases are processed through the GeM portal, which is integrated with IPAS, the Railways' accounting and payment system.

q: In railway stores management, the abbreviation iMMS stands for:

options.A: Indian Material Management System
options.B: Integrated Materials Monitoring System
options.D: Internal Material Movement System

e: iMMS stands for Integrated Material Management System, the computerised system used on Railways for stores/materials management functions.

q: The abbreviation IREPS stands for:

options.A: Indian Railways E-Procurement System
options.B: Indian Railways Emergency Purchase System
options.D: Indian Railways Electronic Payment System

e: IREPS stands for Indian Railways E-Procurement System, the portal through which e-tenders and e-auctions of the Railways are conducted.

q: Condemned/scrap stores on Indian Railways are sold through e-auction conducted on the:

options.A: GeM portal
options.B: IREPS portal
options.D: Railway Board website

e: Condemned and scrap stores are disposed of through e-auction conducted on the IREPS portal, giving wide and transparent competition among scrap buyers.

q: Unserviceable stores are condemned and surveyed off on the recommendation of a:

options.A: Single storekeeper
options.B: Travelling Inspector of Stores
options.D: Survey Committee

e: Unserviceable stores are condemned and surveyed off only on the recommendation of a Survey Committee, which examines and certifies that the stores are unfit for further use.

q: Stores found surplus in one depot are, before being disposed of:

options.A: Sold immediately by auction
options.B: Circulated/offered to other depots and railways which may require them
options.D: Returned to the original supplier

e: Before disposal, surplus stores are circulated and offered to other depots and railways which may need them, so that usable material is utilised within the Railways first.

q: 'Imprest stores' means:

options.A: A fixed quantity of stores held by field officials for petty day-to-day requirements
options.B: Stores kept in the headquarters office for VIP use
options.D: Stores held by contractors at work sites

e: Imprest stores are a fixed, small stock of day-to-day items held by field officials so that petty requirements can be met without indenting on the depot each time.

q: Imprest stores held by a field official are replenished on the basis of:

options.A: A fresh tender for every replenishment
options.B: The account of consumption rendered by the imprest holder
options.D: A narrative report of the Stock Verifier

e: Imprest stock is replenished against the account of consumption rendered by the imprest holder, i.e. only to the extent stores have actually been consumed.

q: The Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) is the quantity for which:

options.A: The purchase price per unit is the lowest
options.B: The consumption of the item is the maximum
options.C: The storage space required is the minimum
options.D: The total of ordering cost and inventory carrying cost is the minimum

e: EOQ is the order quantity at which the total cost - ordering cost plus inventory carrying cost - is at its minimum; ordering more or less raises the total cost.

q: VED analysis of inventory classifies items according to:

options.A: Their annual consumption value
options.B: Their weight and bulk
options.C: The criticality of the item in use (Vital, Essential, Desirable)
options.D: The country of origin of the item

e: VED analysis classifies items by criticality in use - Vital, Essential and Desirable - so that vital items, whose stock-out is most serious, receive the closest attention.

q: FSN analysis of inventory classifies items according to:

options.A: Their rate of consumption/movement — Fast, Slow and Non-moving
options.B: Their purchase price
options.D: Their source of supply

e: FSN analysis groups items by their movement - Fast-moving, Slow-moving and Non-moving - based on the rate of consumption, aiding stock review and disposal decisions.

q:
Inventory carrying cost includes which of the following?
1. Interest on the capital locked up in stock
2. Cost of storage, handling and insurance
3. Losses due to deterioration and obsolescence

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 1 and 2 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

e: Carrying cost comprises all three elements: interest on capital locked up, storage/handling/insurance expenses, and losses from deterioration and obsolescence of stock.

q: The minimum stock level fixed for an item represents:

options.A: The maximum quantity that may be held at any time
options.B: The safety stock below which the balance should not ordinarily fall
options.C: The quantity consumed in one year
options.D: The quantity ordered in one purchase order

e: The minimum stock level is the safety stock - the floor below which the balance should not ordinarily fall, protecting supplies against delays and consumption variations.

q: The 're-order level' of a stock item is the level at which:

options.A: The item is declared surplus
options.B: Stock verification is carried out
options.D: The item is written off from the books

e: The re-order level is the stock point at which fresh procurement action must be initiated, so that new supplies arrive before the stock is exhausted.

q: 'Lead time' in stores procurement means the time taken between:

options.A: Placement of the order and receipt of the material
options.B: Receipt of the material and its issue to the consumer
options.C: Opening of the tender and placement of the order
options.D: Two successive stock verifications

e: Lead time is the total time between placing the purchase order and actually receiving the material, and coverage/re-order levels are fixed with reference to it.

q: The Stores Monthly Summary (SMS) is:

options.A: A summary of tenders opened during the month
options.B: A summary of staff attendance in the stores depot
options.C: A list of surplus stores circulated every month
options.D: A monthly summary of stores transactions (receipts and issues) prepared by each depot, forming the basis for compilation of the stores accounts

e: The Stores Monthly Summary (SMS) summarises each depot's stores transactions (receipts and issues) for the month and forms the basis for compiling the stores accounts.

q: If the closing stores balance (including suspense balances) keeps rising while total issues remain unchanged, the Turnover Ratio will:

options.A: Decrease, showing better inventory control
options.B: Increase, indicating more capital locked up in stock in relation to issues
options.D: Become zero

e: TOR = Closing balance / Total issues. If the closing balance rises while issues stay unchanged, the ratio rises, showing more capital locked up per rupee of issues - poorer inventory control.

q: The differences between physical and book balances reported in a stock sheet are adjusted, after approval of the competent authority, through the:

options.A: Purchase Suspense Account
options.B: Sales Suspense Account
options.D: Traffic Suspense Account

e: Differences between physical and book balances reported in stock sheets are, after approval of the competent authority, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: Stores found physically in excess of the book balance during stock verification are:

options.A: Taken on stock, with the necessary adjustment through the Stock Adjustment Account
options.B: Removed from the depot without any entry
options.C: Treated as the personal property of the storekeeper
options.D: Sold immediately and the proceeds kept in the depot

e: Excess stock found on verification is taken on stock (brought on account), with the corresponding value adjustment passed through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: At the zonal railway headquarters, the stores organisation is headed by the:

options.A: Principal Financial Adviser
options.B: Chief Materials Manager of the division
options.D: Controller of Stores

e: At zonal railway headquarters the stores organisation is headed by the Controller of Stores, the head of the stores department of the railway.

q: The 'credits' anticipated in a Stores Budget represent the:

options.A: Loans taken for purchase of stores
options.B: Refunds received from suppliers
options.C: Value of stores expected to be issued and sold during the year
options.D: Closing balance of stores at the end of the year

e: The 'credits' in a Stores Budget represent the value of stores expected to be issued to consuming departments and sold during the year, set off against the total requirements.

q: 'Vital items' (safety items) of stores are those:

options.A: Which are consumed daily in train operations
options.B: Whose non-availability can affect the safe running of trains
options.C: Which are the costliest items in stock
options.D: Which are imported from abroad

e: Vital items are safety items whose non-availability can affect the safe running of trains, so their stock position is watched most critically.

q: 'Insurance spares' in stores parlance are:

options.A: Spares insured against fire and theft
options.B: Spares supplied free by the manufacturer
options.C: Spares kept by the insurance company
options.D: Costly, slow-moving spares stocked as an insurance against prolonged breakdown of important equipment

e: Insurance spares are costly, slow-moving spares kept purely as an insurance against prolonged breakdown of important equipment, even though they may rarely be used.

q: The storekeeper, as custodian of the stores in his charge, is responsible for:

options.A: Fixing the purchase price of stores
options.B: The safe custody of the stores and the correctness of the balances held by him
options.D: Granting tenders to firms

e: The storekeeper, as custodian, is responsible for the safe custody of the stores in his charge and for the correctness of the balances held by him.

q: Stores transferred from one depot to another depot are priced at:

options.A: The current market rate
options.B: The rate of the last purchase by the receiving depot
options.C: The book value of the material
options.D: A rate fixed by the receiving depot

e: Inter-depot transfers are priced at the book value of the material, so that the value moves between depots without any profit or revaluation.

q: While 'covering' a demand for procurement, the quantity to be ordered is determined mainly with reference to:

options.A: The AAC (Average Annual Consumption) and the prescribed period of coverage
options.B: The balance in the depot bin on that day alone
options.C: The quantity ordered in the previous year alone
options.D: The supplier's minimum order quantity

e: While covering a demand, the quantity to be ordered is worked out mainly from the AAC and the prescribed period of coverage, after allowing for stock in hand and dues.

q: A balance outstanding under Purchase Suspense is finally cleared (liquidated) when:

options.A: The tender for the next purchase is opened
options.B: The financial year comes to an end
options.C: The stock verification of the depot is completed
options.D: The material has been received and the corresponding bill has been paid and linked

e: A Purchase Suspense balance is finally liquidated only when both legs are complete - the material has been received into stock and the corresponding bill has been paid and linked.

q: Bin Cards of a stores depot are maintained by:

options.A: The Accounts Department at headquarters
options.B: The depot storekeeper at the bins
options.D: The supplier of the material

e: Bin Cards are maintained by the depot storekeeper at the bins themselves, recording each receipt and issue as it occurs.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence of stages in stores procurement?

options.A: Purchase Order, Tender, Indent, Tender Committee recommendations
options.B: Indent/Demand, Invitation of tenders, Tender Committee recommendations, Acceptance, Purchase Order
options.C: Tender Committee recommendations, Indent, Purchase Order, Invitation of tenders
options.D: Acceptance, Indent, Invitation of tenders, Purchase Order

e: The correct sequence is: Indent/Demand, invitation of tenders, Tender Committee recommendations, acceptance of the tender, and then issue of the Purchase Order.

q: Firms seeking registration with the Railways for supply of stores are registered:

options.A: For the specific trade groups/items which they manufacture or deal in
options.B: Generally, for all stores items without exception
options.D: Only after they have supplied stores continuously for five years

e: Firms are registered only for the specific trade groups/items they manufacture or deal in, ensuring they are considered for tenders in their proven line of business.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Only registered firms are permitted to participate in open tenders invited by advertisement.
2. Limited tenders for stores are invited from registered/approved firms.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: open tenders advertised publicly can be participated in by firms generally. Statement 2 is true: limited tenders are invited only from registered/approved firms.

q: A firm which indulges in corrupt practices or persistently fails to supply stores can be:

options.A: Fined by the depot storekeeper
options.B: Asked to supply all future orders at half rates
options.C: Ignored, as no action lies against a supplier
options.D: Banned/blacklisted, suspending business dealings with it for the period of the ban

e: A firm guilty of corrupt practices or persistent failure to supply can be banned/blacklisted, suspending all business dealings with it for the period of the ban.

q: The two-packet (two-bid) system of tendering is mandatory in stores procurement for tenders valued above:

options.A: Rs 5 lakh
options.B: Rs 10 lakh
options.D: Rs 5 crore

e: The two-packet (two-bid) system is mandatory for stores tenders valued above Rs 50 lakh, ensuring technical evaluation precedes opening of price bids in high-value cases.

q: Stores tenders on Indian Railways are ordinarily invited through:

options.A: E-tendering on the IREPS portal
options.B: Sealed covers received by post only
options.D: Personal canvassing by depot staff

e: Stores tenders are ordinarily invited through e-tendering on the IREPS portal, which has replaced the manual tendering process on Indian Railways.

q: The reasonableness of the lowest rate received in a stores tender is judged mainly with reference to:

options.A: The highest rate quoted in the tender
options.B: The Last Accepted Rate (LAR), prevailing market rates and the estimated rate
options.C: The rate quoted in the oldest tender on record
options.D: The budget provision available for the item

e: Reasonableness of the lowest rate is judged against the Last Accepted Rate (LAR), prevailing market rates and the estimated rate for the item.

q: Where negotiations become unavoidable in a stores tender, they are held:

options.A: With all the tenderers together
options.B: With the highest tenderer
options.C: Only with the lowest tenderer (L1), in exceptional circumstances
options.D: With the members of the tender committee

e: Negotiations, where unavoidable, are held only with the lowest tenderer (L1) and only in exceptional circumstances, to preserve the sanctity of the tender process.

q: Acceptance of a tender must be communicated to the tenderer:

options.A: At any time, even years after the opening of the tender
options.B: Only after the material has been supplied
options.D: Within the validity period of the offer; thereafter only with the tenderer's consent

e: Acceptance must reach the tenderer within the validity period of his offer; after its expiry, acceptance is possible only with the tenderer's consent.

q: Under a rate contract, the actual supplies are obtained by:

options.A: Placing supply orders on the firm from time to time during the currency of the contract, as and when required
options.B: A single supply of the entire estimated quantity at the very start
options.C: Inviting fresh tenders for every requirement
options.D: Direct purchase from the open market

e: Under a rate contract, supplies are obtained by placing supply orders on the firm from time to time during the contract's currency, as and when material is required.

q: Stores required by the Railways are ordinarily procured to:

options.A: Specifications framed separately by each depot
options.B: The supplier's own trade specification
options.C: Indian Railway Standard (IRS) specifications or RDSO specifications/drawings
options.D: The specifications of the previous supplier

e: Stores are procured to Indian Railway Standard (IRS) specifications or RDSO specifications/drawings, ensuring uniform quality across all railways.

q: Security Deposit is taken from the successful tenderer in a stores contract primarily to:

options.A: Earn interest for the Railway
options.B: Secure due fulfilment of the contract; it is refunded after satisfactory completion of the supplies
options.C: Meet the cost of inspection of stores
options.D: Pay the tender advertisement charges

e: Security Deposit secures due fulfilment of the contract by the supplier and is refunded after the supplies are satisfactorily completed.

q: Under the warranty clause of a stores contract, if stores are found defective within the warranty period, the supplier is required to:

options.A: Pay a fixed fine and take no further action
options.B: Supply fresh material only against a new purchase order
options.C: Repair the material at the Railway's cost
options.D: Replace or repair the defective stores free of cost

e: Under the warranty clause, stores found defective within the warranty period must be replaced or repaired by the supplier free of cost to the Railway.

q: Liquidated damages in a stores contract are:

options.A: A genuine pre-estimate of the loss the Railway may suffer due to delayed supply, and not a penalty
options.B: A penalty imposed at the discretion of the storekeeper
options.C: Payable by the Railway to the supplier for late payment of bills
options.D: Recoverable only through a court of law

e: Liquidated damages are a genuine pre-estimate of the loss from delayed supply, agreed in advance in the contract - not an arbitrary penalty.

q: Extension of the delivery period in a stores contract is granted by the competent authority:

options.A: Automatically on expiry of the original period
options.B: Only by the Railway Board in all cases
options.C: With or without liquidated damages, depending on whether the delay is attributable to the supplier
options.D: Only if the supplier deposits the full contract value in advance

e: Extension of the delivery period is granted with or without liquidated damages, depending on whether the delay is attributable to the supplier or to other causes.

q: Where pre-despatch inspection is prescribed in a purchase order, the supplier may despatch the material only after:

options.A: Receiving full payment of the bill amount
options.B: An inspection certificate is issued by the inspecting authority
options.D: The consignee visits the firm's premises

e: Where pre-despatch inspection is prescribed, the supplier can despatch material only after the inspecting authority has inspected it and issued an inspection certificate.

q: For stores items notified as safety/critical items, procurement is made only from sources approved by:

options.A: NSIC
options.B: GeM
options.D: RDSO

e: For notified safety/critical items, procurement is restricted to RDSO-approved sources, since RDSO is the authority that approves sources for such items.

q: Inspection of purchased stores on behalf of the Railways, where so prescribed, may be carried out by:

options.A: RITES, acting as an inspection agency
options.B: The supplier's own staff, without any independent check
options.D: The Railway Protection Force

e: Inspection of purchased stores, where prescribed, may be carried out by RITES, which acts as an inspection agency on behalf of the Railways.

q: Form DS-8 used in railway stores depots is the:

options.A: Issue Note
options.B: Bin Card
options.D: Stock Sheet

e: Form DS-8 is the Receipt Note used in stores depots for recording the receipt and acceptance of material into stock.

q: In a purchase order, the 'consignee' is:

options.A: The firm on whom the order is placed
options.B: The depot/official nominated to receive the material and account for its receipt
options.C: The officer who accepts the tender
options.D: The Accounts officer who passes the bill

e: The consignee in a purchase order is the depot or official nominated to receive the material and account for its receipt - not the supplier or the accepting officer.

q: Material received at a depot which does not conform to the specification/sample is:

options.A: Accepted into stock at a reduced rate fixed by the storekeeper
options.B: Issued to the user department with a warning
options.C: Retained in stock until it is somehow consumed
options.D: Rejected under a rejection advice; the supplier must remove the rejected material and supply conforming material

e: Material not conforming to specification/sample is rejected under a rejection advice; the supplier must remove it and supply conforming material in its place.

q: A supplier's bill can be passed for payment only in respect of stores which have been:

options.A: Merely ordered from the firm
options.B: Despatched by the firm
options.C: Received, inspected and accepted into stock
options.D: Inspected at the firm's premises before despatch

e: A bill can be passed only for stores actually received, inspected and accepted into stock; mere ordering or despatch does not create a liability for payment.

q: Fresh stock of an item is received at a rate different from the existing book rate. The issue rate of the item is then revised to:

options.A: A new book average rate worked out on the total value and total quantity of the combined balance
options.B: The rate of the latest purchase, ignoring the old balance
options.C: The higher of the two rates
options.D: The original book rate, which can never be changed

e: When fresh stock is received at a different rate, the issue rate is revised to a new book average rate based on the total value and total quantity of the combined (old + new) balance.

q: Under uniform pricing of stores on a railway:

options.A: All items in stock carry the same price
options.B: The issue (book) rate of an item is the same in all the depots of the railway
options.C: All suppliers are required to quote identical rates
options.D: Issue prices are revised every day

e: Uniform pricing means the issue (book) rate of an item is the same in all depots of the railway, so issues are valued identically everywhere on that railway.

q: A PL (Price Ledger) Number allotted to a stores item consists of:

options.A: 4 digits
options.B: 5 digits
options.D: 8 digits

e: A PL (Price Ledger) Number allotted to a stores item consists of 8 digits, which codify the group, sub-group and the item's identity.
